n75553f1ba48.s: The advice given by the UPSC to the government is:
n75553f1ba48.x: UPSC advice is only advisory; even action taken without consulting the UPSC is not invalid for that reason alone.

nindian-polity-52-45.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by:
nindian-polity-52-45.x: Parliament prescribes the qualifications by law (Finance Commission Act, 1951); the President only constitutes the Commission.

ne9bc8ba31c0.s: A member of a Joint State Public Service Commission holds office for six years or until the age of:
ne9bc8ba31c0.x: A JSPSC member, like an SPSC member, retires at 62; the age of 65 applies to UPSC members.

nindian-polity-52-15.s: How many members, including the Chairman, does the Finance Commission have?
nindian-polity-52-15.x: The Finance Commission has five members including the Chairman; 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha) describes the PAC.

n2f30372e163.s: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Chairman must have experience in:
n2f30372e163.x: The Act requires the Chairman to have experience in public affairs; government finance and accounts is a member's qualification, and no post is for a monetary policy expert.

n5ee6941f5f4.s: The Finance Commission is best described as a:
o: Statutory body under the Finance Ministry
n5ee6941f5f4.x: Under Article 280 the Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body, constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.

n46b3c40c0a2.s: The term of office of the members of the Finance Commission is specified by the:
n46b3c40c0a2.x: The President specifies the term and members are eligible for reappointment; the Constitution does not fix one term.

nec998d39813.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the report of the 16th Finance Commission?
o: It was submitted to the President in November 2025
It was tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026
The Centre rejected its recommended devolution in the Budget 2026-27 speech
It retained the States' share in the divisible pool at 41%
nec998d39813.x: The Centre accepted, not rejected, the 16th FC's devolution in the Budget 2026-27 speech; the other statements are correct.

n4553afa2242.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31)?
o: The disaster corpus is about Rs 2.04 lakh crore
State deficits are capped at 3% of GSDP
Disaster funds are shared 75:25 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
n4553afa2242.x: The ratios are reversed: disaster funds are shared 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for the others.

nindian-polity-26-10.s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President:
o: Only on a resolution of Parliament
nindian-polity-26-10.x: The Finance Commission is not permanent; it is set up every fifth year or earlier, and it is an independent body.

n3b96d4962e0.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was:
o: Included in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
Promised in Parliament in 2014 but not included in the AP Reorganisation Act
n3b96d4962e0.x: SCS was a parliamentary promise of 2014, not a provision of the AP Reorganisation Act; the Centre gave special assistance instead.

nindian-polity-80-45.s: The administrative expenses of the CAG, including the salaries and pensions of his staff, are:
o: Voted annually by the Lok Sabha
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Met from the Contingency Fund of India
Voted by both Houses of Parliament
nindian-polity-80-45.x: The CAG's administrative expenses, including salaries, allowances and pensions of him and his staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund and so are non-votable.

nindian-polity-80-12.s: Who causes the CAG's audit report on Union accounts to be laid before both Houses of Parliament?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-80-12.x: The CAG submits the Union report to the President, who causes it to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

nindian-polity-78-28.s: Which of the following retires at the age of 62 years?
nindian-polity-78-28.x: High Court judges and State PSC members retire at 62; Supreme Court judges, UPSC members, the CAG and Election Commissioners are in the 65 group.

nindian-polity-78-35.s: The tenure and retirement of the CAG are governed by Article 148(3) and the:
o: CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
nindian-polity-78-35.x: The CAG's tenure comes from Article 148(3) and the CAG Act, 1971; the Election Commission Act governs the Election Commissioners.

nindian-polity-80-53.s: What role does the CAG play once his audit reports reach the Public Accounts Committee?
o: He assists the Committee in examining them
He presents the Committee's report to the Speaker
nindian-polity-80-53.x: Audit reports go first to the President or Governor and then to the legislature; the CAG then helps the PAC examine them.

nc66f4f5926d.s: Which of the following is wholly audited by private auditors, with no supplementary audit by the CAG?
nc66f4f5926d.x: The RBI is wholly audited by private auditors; DVC and ONGC are audited directly by the CAG, and the Central Warehousing Corporation gets a CAG supplementary audit.

nindian-polity-80-34.s: India's CAG audits only after expenditure, without any control over the issue of money from the treasury, and so functions merely as:
nindian-polity-80-34.x: The Indian CAG is only an Auditor General, auditing after expenditure, so he exercises no prior control over treasury issues.

nindian-polity-80-17.s: With regard to irregular expenditure, the CAG can:
nindian-polity-80-17.x: The CAG cannot disallow expenditure, enforce recovery or punish; he only reports to the legislature.

nindian-polity-80-59.s: Unlike India's CAG, the Comptroller and Auditor General of which country controls the issue of money from the treasury?
nindian-polity-80-59.x: The British Comptroller and Auditor General controls the issue of money from the treasury, whereas India's CAG is only an Auditor General.

nindian-polity-80-3.s: Who described the CAG as the most important officer under the Constitution of India?
nindian-polity-80-3.x: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the CAG the most important officer under the Constitution.

new.s: Which Article provides for regulations on the conditions of service of members of Public Service Commissions?
new.x: Article 318 deals with regulations on conditions of service; 316 is appointment and term, 319 the post-retirement bar, 320 functions.

new.s: Which Article bars members of Public Service Commissions from holding office after ceasing to be members?
new.x: Article 319 contains the post-retirement bar; 317 is removal, 321 extension of functions and 322 expenses.

new.s: Which Act first provided for a Public Service Commission in India?
new.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a Public Service Commission; the 1935 Act created the Federal PSC.

new.s: The Federal Public Service Commission and provincial PSCs were provided for by the:
new.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for a Federal PSC and provincial PSCs; the Federal PSC became the UPSC in 1950.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the UPSC:
1. The Lee Commission recommended a Public Service Commission in 1924.
2. The first Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926.
3. The Federal PSC became the UPSC on 15 August 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Lee Commission recommended it in 1924 and the PSC was set up on 1 October 1926; the Federal PSC became the UPSC on 26 January 1950, not in 1947.

new.s: Under which Article did the members of the Federal PSC continue as members of the UPSC in 1950?
new.x: On 26 January 1950 the Federal PSC became the UPSC and its members continued under Article 378.

new.s: When the office of the UPSC Chairman is vacant, an Acting Chairman is appointed by the:
new.x: The President appoints an Acting Chairman when the Chairman's office is vacant or he is absent.

new.s: The usual strength of the UPSC, including the Chairman, is:
new.x: The President fixes the UPSC's strength, usually 9-11 including the Chairman; the Constitution does not fix the number.

new.s: During the Supreme Court inquiry into misbehaviour, a member of a State PSC may be suspended by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: For an SPSC member the Governor may suspend during the inquiry; removal itself is by the President.

new.s: What role does Parliament play in removing a UPSC member for misbehaviour?
o: It must pass an address by special majority
It must pass a resolution by simple majority
It refers the case to the Supreme Court
new.x: The President removes after a Supreme Court inquiry whose advice is binding; Parliament plays no part.

new.s: After appointment, the conditions of service of a member of a Public Service Commission:
o: Cannot be varied to his disadvantage
Can be varied by the President at any time
Can be varied by a resolution of Parliament
Can be varied by the Chairman
new.x: As a safeguard of independence, a member's conditions of service cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.

new.s: After ceasing to hold office, the Chairman of the UPSC is eligible for:
o: No further employment under the Government of India or any State
Any office under a State government
new.x: Under Article 319 the UPSC Chairman can hold nothing under the Government of India or any State.

new.s: After ceasing to hold office, a member (other than the Chairman) of the UPSC can be appointed as:
o: Chairman of the UPSC or of a State PSC
Any post under the Government of India
Member of a State PSC only
new.x: A UPSC member may later become UPSC Chairman or SPSC Chairman only, under Article 319.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a safeguard of the independence of Public Service Commissions?
o: Their expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund
Members can be removed only on the grounds stated in the Constitution
Members are eligible for reappointment to the same office
Conditions of service cannot be varied to a member's disadvantage
new.x: There is no reappointment to the same office; the other three are constitutional safeguards.

new.s: The UPSC is consulted on temporary appointments only if they are likely to last more than:
new.x: Temporary appointments of more than one year are referred to the UPSC; posts of less than one year are not.

new.s: Regulations excluding posts from the purview of the UPSC are made by the:
new.x: The President (Governor for an SPSC) may exclude posts by regulations, which are laid before the legislature for 14 days.

new.s: Besides the UPSC, which body is also consulted on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants?
new.x: The CVC (1964, statutory in 2003) is also consulted on disciplinary matters, though the UPSC has the edge.

new.s: According to the Supreme Court, selection of a candidate by the UPSC:
o: Gives a legal right to the post
Confers no right to the post
Binds the government to appoint within a year
Can be cancelled only by Parliament
new.x: The Supreme Court has held that selection by the UPSC confers no right to the post.

new.s: The UPSC presents its annual report to the:
new.x: The UPSC reports to the President, who lays it before both Houses with a memorandum on advice not accepted.

new.s: A member of a Joint State Public Service Commission submits his resignation to the:
new.x: JSPSC members are appointed, suspended and removed by the President and resign to the President, not the Governor.

new.s: Which of the following is a statutory body and not a constitutional one?
new.x: A JSPSC is created by an Act of Parliament, so it is statutory; the UPSC and SPSCs are constitutional bodies under Article 315.

new.s: Which pair of States once had a Joint State Public Service Commission?
new.x: Punjab and Haryana once had a JSPSC; after 2014 Telangana got its own TSPSC.

new.s: The present strength of the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission is:
new.x: The APPSC has a Chairman and 9 Members, a strength enhanced in 1994.

new.s: After the 2014 bifurcation, the headquarters of the APPSC moved to:
new.x: After 2014 the APPSC continued for residuary Andhra Pradesh with its headquarters moved to Vijayawada.

new.s: Which committee recommended the three-stage Civil Services Examination of prelims, mains and interview?
new.x: The Kothari Committee (1976) recommended the three-stage examination.

new.s: The essay paper was added to the Civil Services Examination on the recommendation of the:
new.x: The Satish Chandra Committee (1989) added the essay paper.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (committee on the Civil Services Examination - year) is correctly matched?
new.x: Kothari was 1976; Satish Chandra 1989, Y.K. Alagh 2001 and B.S. Baswan 2015-16.

new.s: Article 290 of the Constitution relates to:
new.x: Article 290 deals with pensions; the Finance Commission is under Article 280.

new.s: The Finance Commission submits its report to the:
new.x: The Finance Commission reports to the President, not to NITI Aayog; the President lays it before each House under Article 281.

new.s: For summoning persons and requiring production of documents, the Finance Commission has the powers of a:
new.x: The Finance Commission has the powers of a civil court, which makes it quasi-judicial.

new.s: The net proceeds of the divisible pool of Central taxes are certified by the:
new.x: The divisible pool is gross tax revenue minus cesses, surcharges and cost of collection, and the net amount is certified by the CAG.

new.s: The Finance Commission suggests measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for Panchayats and Municipalities on the basis of recommendations of the:
new.x: Under Article 280(3) the measures for local bodies are based on the recommendations of the State Finance Commission.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?
o: Recommending distribution of net tax proceeds between Centre and States
Recommending principles of grants-in-aid to States
Suggesting measures to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities
new.x: The Finance Commission does not fix GST rates or release funds; it only recommends.

new.s: Who was the Chairman of the 10th Finance Commission?
new.x: K.C. Pant chaired the 10th FC (1995-2000); A.M. Khusro the 11th and C. Rangarajan the 12th.

new.s: The 13th Finance Commission (2010-15) was chaired by:
new.x: Vijay Kelkar chaired the 13th FC; Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th and N.K. Singh the 15th.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Finance Commission - Chairman) is correctly matched?
new.x: A.M. Khusro chaired the 11th FC; the 14th was Y.V. Reddy, the 16th Arvind Panagariya and the 10th K.C. Pant.

new.s: The share of States in Central taxes recommended by the 13th Finance Commission was:
new.x: The 13th FC recommended 32%, which the 14th FC raised to 42%.

new.s: The 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution' with a States' share of 29% is associated with which Finance Commission?
new.x: The 10th FC (K.C. Pant) recommended 29% under the Alternative Scheme of Devolution.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Finance Commission - States' share) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The 15th FC cut the share to 41%; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: The award period of the 13th Finance Commission was:
new.x: The 13th FC covered 2010-15; 2005-10 was the 12th and 2015-20 the 14th.

new.s: Who was the Chairman of the 14th Finance Commission?
new.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC (2015-20).

new.s: Which criterion carried the highest weight (50%) in the 14th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution?
new.x: Income distance had 50%; population 1971 17.5%, area 15% and forest cover 7.5%.

new.s: The 14th Finance Commission used population data of which years?
new.x: The 14th FC used both 1971 and 2011 population; the 15th FC used 2011 only.

new.s: The 15th Finance Commission used the population data of:
new.x: The 15th FC used only the 2011 population, not 1971.

new.s: The 15th Finance Commission reduced the States' share from 42% to 41% because of:
o: The change in the status of Jammu and Kashmir
new.x: The 15th FC cut the vertical share to 41% due to the change in J&K's status.

new.s: The total local-body grants recommended by the 15th Finance Commission were about:
new.x: The 15th FC recommended Rs 4.36 lakh crore for local bodies; Rs 7.91 lakh crore is the 16th FC figure.

new.s: Horizontal devolution refers to the distribution of tax proceeds:
o: Between the Centre and the States
Between the Union and Union Territories
new.x: Horizontal devolution is among States by criteria and weights; vertical devolution is between the Centre and States.

new.s: What weight did the 15th Finance Commission give to income distance?
new.x: The 15th FC gave income distance 45%; the 16th FC 42.5% and the 14th FC 50%.

new.s: Which horizontal devolution criterion was dropped by the 16th Finance Commission?
new.x: The 16th FC dropped tax and fiscal effort and added contribution to GDP.

new.s: The 'Contribution to GDP' criterion was first used by which Finance Commission?
new.x: The 16th FC was the first to use contribution to GDP, with a weight of 10%.

new.s: Who is the Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
new.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; T. Rabi Sankar is one of its members.

new.s: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on:
new.x: The 16th FC was constituted on 31 December 2023; 27 November 2017 is the 15th FC and 2 January 2013 the 14th.

new.s: The total grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission amount to:
new.x: Total grants are Rs 9.47 lakh crore; Rs 7.91 lakh crore is for local bodies and Rs 2.04 lakh crore the disaster corpus.

new.s: Grants-in-aid to needy States on Finance Commission recommendations are given under Article:
new.x: Article 275 grants are for needy States; Article 280 sets up the FC and 290 deals with pensions.

new.s: Special Category Status was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the:
new.x: SCS came in 1969 on the 5th FC's recommendation (Mahavir Tyagi); funds were allotted by the Gadgil formula.

new.s: The first States to get Special Category Status were:
o: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Assam
new.x: Assam, Jammu & Kashmir and Nagaland were the first Special Category States.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for Special Category Status?
new.x: SCS criteria include hilly terrain, low density or large tribal share, strategic border location and backwardness, not high income.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's share of the States' pool under the 16th Finance Commission is:
new.x: AP's share is 4.217% under the 16th FC; it was 4.305% under the 14th and 4.047% under the 15th.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's share of the States' pool:
1. It fell from the 14th to the 15th Finance Commission.
2. It is higher under the 16th than under the 15th Finance Commission.
3. It is higher under the 16th than under the 14th Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: AP's share went 4.305% (14th) to 4.047% (15th) to 4.217% (16th), so 1 and 2 are correct; 4.217% is below 4.305%, so 3 is wrong.

new.s: According to the AP Finance Minister, the loss to Andhra Pradesh from the ending of revenue-deficit grants is up to:
new.x: AP said it lost up to Rs 38,000 crore when revenue-deficit grants were dropped by the 16th FC.

new.s: The qualifications of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are:
o: The same as those of a Supreme Court judge
new.x: The Constitution sets no qualifications for the CAG.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a safeguard of the CAG's independence?
o: His salary is equal to that of a Supreme Court judge
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
He is barred from further office under the Government of India or any State
His expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
new.x: The CAG does not hold office at the President's pleasure; he is removed only like a Supreme Court judge.

new.s: After the separation of accounts from audit in 1976, Union accounts are compiled by the:
new.x: Since 1 March 1976 the CGA in the Finance Ministry keeps Union accounts; the CAG still keeps most State accounts.

new.s: Which audit by the CAG looks at wisdom, faithfulness and economy and flags extravagance?
new.x: Propriety audit is discretionary and flags extravagance; legal and regulatory (compliance) and financial attest audits are obligatory.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (type of CAG audit - nature) is correctly matched?
new.x: Propriety and performance audits are discretionary; legal and regulatory and financial attest audits are obligatory.

new.s: The Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) is audited by:
o: Private auditors, with a supplementary audit by the CAG
Private auditors wholly, with no role for the CAG
new.x: LIC and RBI are wholly audited by private auditors; IFCI gets a CAG supplementary audit and DVC and ONGC are audited directly.

new.s: Since 1967 the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been taken from the:
new.x: The PAC Chairman, appointed by the Speaker, has been from the Opposition since 1967.

new.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in:
new.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.

new.s: CAG audit reports relating to the accounts of Andhra Pradesh are submitted to the:
o: Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly
new.x: Under Article 151(2) State audit reports go to the Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature.

new.s: According to the CAG's State Finances report for 2022-23, Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts were about:
new.x: AP's revenue receipts were Rs 1,57,768 crore, of which own tax revenue was Rs 78,026 crore.

new.s: In the CAG's 2022-23 State Finances report, own tax revenue formed about what part of Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts?
new.x: Own tax revenue of Rs 78,026 crore was about half of revenue receipts of Rs 1,57,768 crore.

new.s: The CAG's 2012 report on coal block allocation put the loss at about:
new.x: The coal blocks report (2012) put the loss at Rs 1.86 lakh crore; Rs 1.76 lakh crore was the 2G figure.
